functional_scaffold.question: Around the function/content band, do stopword run lengths and sentence openings occupy repeatable collective regions across genres?
functional_scaffold.definition_control: The first two coordinates share FUNCTION_WORDS counts and are largely the transform p/(1-p). This band is a measurement control, not a novel relation. Runs and sentence openings use spaCy STOP, a different lexicon, and are the actual response investigation.
functional_scaffold.interaction: The function/content curve is largely fixed by shared counts. The actual question is how stopword runs and sentence openings respond around it. These additional responses vary by genre and do not yet establish a common class-specific reaction.

genres.email: AI occupies a shorter segment of the function/content curve and a compact, rising run-mean response. Human covers much broader function share and run lengths. Much of the contrast is occupied anchor range.
genres.review: AI has distinct occupied curve segments and tight run/opening configurations. Human fills a broader run-response band. This is a local branching lead; the mathematical function/content curve itself is shared.
genres.legal: There is substantial shared function-share support, with AI run means often below Human and differently distributed openings. Overlap is broad and the first two members are definition-related.
genres.abstracts: AI and Human mostly occupy different function-share regions. Low AI run mean and opening response therefore cannot be read as a conditional difference at equal anchors from this overview.
genres.articles: AI occupies a lower/shorter function-share segment and a rising run-mean cloud. Human has a broader, higher cloud; remaining common-anchor behaviour needs focused study.
genres.papers: Both classes follow the same count-derived scaffold, with overlapping run/opening values. Sparse points do not establish a class-specific collective reaction.

clause_packaging.question: When two per-sentence clause counts form a wedge or corridor, how are tree depth, sentence length, coordination and passive subjects placed around it?
clause_packaging.definition_control: Clause proxies overlap in ccomp counts, and per-sentence denominators are shared. Coordination uses an alphabetic-word denominator. Count/denominator geometry alone is not a class-specific discovery.
clause_packaging.interaction: The two clause proxies form a wedge whose depth and sentence-length response is more constrained in several AI panels. In the length/depth view, legal and articles suggest a lower AI depth corridor, but some other genres largely share the relation. This extends the earlier syntax investigation.

genres.email: Clause proxies overlap in a wedge. AI forms a compact length/depth corridor, but much of it overlaps the Human short-sentence relation; Human covers more extremes.
genres.review: AI produces a few clause/depth branches at a narrow sentence-length range. Human is broader; this local structure does not imply a universal branch count.
genres.legal: Both classes have a broad clause wedge, with AI often in a lower depth corridor at overlapping sentence lengths. Outliers and overlap remain, and overlapping clause-count definitions contribute to the wedge.
genres.abstracts: AI has lower clause/depth/length support overall. Its depth relation rises through a narrower length range; some Human short-length points overlap, so a new conditional rule remains unresolved.
genres.articles: At shared sentence lengths the AI depth corridor appears lower than much of Human. Human clause/depth response also fans upward. This is a promising local extension of the existing syntax family.
genres.papers: Length and depth occupy different ranges with few points. The overlapping range is too sparse to distinguish recurrence from source/length composition.

nominal_packaging.question: Does the noun/compound arrangement support a recurrent modifier and proper-noun configuration, with different dependency reach and grammatical-sequence entropy?
nominal_packaging.definition_control: Noun and proper-noun ratios overlap by definition; dependency proportions use all spaCy tokens rather than alphabetic words. Look for conditional arrangement, not isolated noun abundance.
nominal_packaging.interaction: Nouns and compounds form a scaffold while adjectival modifiers and proper-noun share change around it. Several Human high-noun points have low modification and high proper-name context; AI can occupy a higher-modifier configuration. Review changes that arrangement, and article clouds overlap strongly.

genres.email: AI has a compact noun/compound scaffold with higher adjectival modification than many Human points. Human high-noun/low-modifier points have large proper-noun markers. Name/source composition is a concrete explanation to investigate.
genres.review: AI splits into low-noun modifier branches, while Human has a broad modifier fan and extremes. This is a local arrangement, not the same directional pattern as email/legal.
genres.legal: The noun/compound scaffold overlaps, but AI modifier response is often higher. Human high-noun/low-modifier points and proper-name context remain important; a same-support rule is not established.
genres.abstracts: Both classes form a rising compound scaffold, while modifier response tends to fall with noun share and overlaps strongly. AI occupies a somewhat shifted modifier region; shared definitions and proper-name mix remain explanations.
genres.articles: Noun/compound and noun/modifier configurations overlap broadly once the Human extremes are visible. No clean new recurring geometric distinction is resolved.
genres.papers: AI modifiers often lie higher than Human within the noun range, but the 23-per-class points and source uncertainty make this descriptive only.

repetition_diversity.question: As lexical bigram and trigram variety move together, do repeated phrases, POS entropy and lexical variety organize into different branches or bands?
repetition_diversity.definition_control: Type counts share document length and lexical tokens. Top phrase frequencies are normalized by alphabetic-word count, not the number of ngrams. POS entropy uses a different token sequence.
repetition_diversity.title: Phrase-repetition branch occupancy with grammatical-entropy response
repetition_diversity.interaction: Bigram and trigram type counts form a length-related scaffold. The two normalized maximum phrase frequencies form proportional ray families around that scaffold; POS entropy and lexical variety occupy different parts of the resulting arrangement. AI often concentrates on a smaller set of visible branches, while Human also has rays. The POS response is generally lower in the comparable type-count region, connecting this group to R02 rather than proving a separate independent mechanism.
repetition_diversity.capture_requirements: Represent the joint branch occupancy of both repetition scales together with type-count context and POS response. Preserve shared rays, zero/repetition boundaries, the legal overlap and the locally clustered reviews. Separate branch existence imposed by integer counts from class differences in their occupancy. Do not force one universal frequency ratio.
repetition_diversity.exceptions: Human data also has exact rays. Legal has strong shared ray geometry, email has considerable overlap, and papers do not reveal stable branch structure. Common document-length denominators and integer maxima can explain much of the scaffolding; occupancy differences still need source/count controls.

genres.email: Both classes follow the type-count diagonal and the raw repetition rays. AI concentrates on several thin rays and a compact type-count interval, while Human includes broader length support and dispersed off-ray points. POS entropy is lower in much of the AI type-count region, but repeated-frequency rays alone do not separate the classes.
genres.review: AI occupies a narrow type-count interval with several repeat-frequency branches and a local POS-entropy cluster. Human spans much more of the scaffold and also forms rays. The strong AI local arrangement is real in the graph, but does not establish that the same branch count or slope survives genre.
genres.legal: Human and AI both show pronounced proportional repetition rays; their overlap directly contradicts a claim that ray existence is uniquely AI. AI has a low-entropy branch in the shared type-count region and additional entropy spread at larger counts. Retain this as a difficult shared-geometry case.
genres.abstracts: The AI repetition view concentrates on a few thin rays, while Human fills more intermediate branches. In the common type-count range, AI POS entropy lies mostly below the Human cloud, with overlapping extremes. One low-count AI outlier remains visible in the complete companion.
genres.articles: AI gives a clear small fan of thin repetition rays; Human has a broader set of branch locations at the same small frequencies. AI POS entropy stays lower over a broad shared type-count range, although the highest-count AI points are sparse. The type-count relation itself is a shared length/count scaffold.
genres.papers: The 23-per-class clouds do not resolve a stable repetition-ray family. AI POS entropy is lower in much of the comparable large type-count range, but branch occupancy is unresolved. Do not extrapolate the article fan to papers.

stance_expression.question: Do uncertainty and hedging form a scaffold around which modality, negation and assertive language show recurring class-specific configurations?
stance_expression.definition_control: Hedge, booster and certainty features count lowercase substrings, with possible lexical overlap and multiple hits. Zeros and count strata are real measured values, not smooth psychological traits.
stance_expression.interaction: Hedging, uncertainty and modality form ray families, while booster/certainty responses show additional rays and zero masses. AI often occupies concentrated ray subsets across the five large genres. Human also has rays; shared word-count denominators and substring-count lexicons can produce the geometry.

genres.email: AI has clearer concentrated rays in uncertainty/modality and booster/certainty views. Human has zero masses and some shared rays plus more dispersed points; no unique ray identity is established.
genres.review: AI forms a few disconnected stance clusters with coordinated modality and assertive responses. Human is broad and also quantized. Treat this as a local mixture rather than a single smooth relation.
genres.legal: AI occupies prominent proportional rays, but Human also has strong rays and zero-axis masses. Levels of modality and lexicon use change, so a uniform direction or branch count is inappropriate.
genres.abstracts: AI occupies a small subset of the ray arrangement with much overlap along the zero axes. Human has more diffuse nonzero configurations. Sparse counts and shared denominators are material explanations.
genres.articles: AI has a particularly clear small fan in both uncertainty/modality and booster/certainty views, while Human includes more intermediate placements. Count/length and lexicon audits must precede a structural novelty claim.
genres.papers: The small clouds do not resolve a recurring ray arrangement. Lower AI modality for many points is a marginal observation, not sufficient evidence of a multi-member pattern.

sentence_rhythm.question: As mean and median sentence length form a band, do middle spread and extrema form a constrained envelope in one class, and does question usage occupy particular parts of that envelope?
sentence_rhythm.definition_control: All length summaries use the same sentence-length list and satisfy ordering constraints. A mean/median diagonal alone is not novel. Source truncation and sentence segmentation can shape the envelope.
sentence_rhythm.title: Sentence spread and tail containment around a central-length band
sentence_rhythm.interaction: Mean and median sentence lengths form the two-member central band. IQR and maximum sentence length occupy a joint response envelope around it; minimum length provides a fifth context. The AI response is often lower and more contained, rather than a fixed difference between two means. Question-sentence ratio was inspected as a sixth member but has not shown a necessary recurring role.
sentence_rhythm.capture_requirements: Preserve the joint IQR/maximum envelope conditional on both mean and median; retain overlapping short emails, legal spread, discrete review tail levels, changing genre support, Human examples with small spread, and AI exceptions. Do not summarize this as universal low AI variability or claim all six features are necessary.
sentence_rhythm.exceptions: Short emails overlap strongly; legal regions overlap with large-tail AI examples. Several longer windows contain no AI tuples. Articles have only 11 AI representatives in the middle region. Papers are sparse and descriptive.

genres.email: The full cloud gives a strong compactness impression, but the shared short mean/median region has 145 Human and 365 AI representatives with substantial joint IQR/maximum overlap. In the middle region (69 Human/121 AI), Human extends farther in spread and maximum while AI occupies a lower tail band. There are no AI tuples in the longer region. Treat short emails as a material counterexample to a strong local separation claim.
genres.review: All 454 AI representatives occupy the short region. Their maximum/IQR response sits on a few low, discrete tail levels, whereas 259 Human representatives in that same broad region form a wider fan and overlap its lower part. The middle and longer regions contain Human only. The low tail levels are a local review form of the envelope, not a branch count to impose on every genre.
genres.legal: All three regions have both classes: 50/104, 248/288 and 135/88 Human/AI representatives. AI often occupies a lower and narrower portion of the IQR/maximum envelope, especially in the middle region, but overlap is extensive and some AI examples have long maxima. The longer-region two-response clouds overlap; a universal tail cutoff would misdescribe this genre.
genres.abstracts: The two classes occupy different parts of the mean/median band overall. The middle region provides 313 Human and 83 AI tuples: AI occupies a lower IQR/maximum area while Human extends upward and right, with overlap. The short region has only 30 Human against 413 AI, and the longer region has no AI. This supports an envelope lead but does not provide equal anchor distributions.
genres.articles: The short region (144 Human/440 AI) retains a visibly lower AI IQR/maximum envelope, with overlapping low-tail Human examples. The middle region has 334 Human but only 11 AI, so its apparent continuation is weakly supported. There are no AI tuples in the longer region. The full-genre contrast partly includes different central-length occupancy.
genres.papers: No tuples occupy the short region. The middle region has 7 Human and 21 AI; Human maxima extend above the AI cloud, with overlap. Only 2 AI versus 16 Human occupy the longer region. These small, source-unresolved samples illustrate the possible envelope but cannot establish recurrence.

modifier_allocation.question: Do adjective/adjectival-modifier and adverb/adverbial-modifier bands form a repeatable collective allocation, with suffix and tree-depth responses?
modifier_allocation.definition_control: POS and dependency features can describe overlapping tokens and use different denominators. A suffix is not an exact POS tag. Look for response structure beyond these shared counts.
modifier_allocation.title: Collective allocation between adjectival and adverbial bands
modifier_allocation.interaction: Adjective POS and adjectival dependency proportions form one band; adverb POS and adverbial dependency proportions form another. The candidate is their collective allocation, with LY-suffix and tree-depth context. Several AI genres occupy a higher adjectival and lower adverbial region, with thin lower edges or near-zero strips, while review contains a different multi-branch arrangement. The two within-pair correlations are largely shared measurement structure.
modifier_allocation.capture_requirements: Preserve both grammatical bands together, branch/strip occupancy and the review reversal. Distinguish a POS/dependency relation shared by both classes from the candidate allocation between bands. Do not treat near-zero ADV with nonzero advmod as an error or an authorship rule; these annotation categories can differ.
modifier_allocation.exceptions: Review has high-adverb branches and is an explicit exception to a uniform low-adverb rule. Article adverb/dependency bands overlap strongly. Email and legal retain broad overlap, so shared-support conditioning remains unresolved. No recurring necessity has been established for LY suffix or tree depth.

genres.email: Both POS/dependency bands are visible. AI occupies a higher adjectival range and several thin adverb/dependency lower edges, while Human spans broader low-adjective configurations. At overlapping adverb coordinates the clouds also overlap; this is not a demonstrated conditional separation.
genres.review: The AI adjective/dependency and adverb/dependency configurations split into distinct local branches. Several have high adverb and advmod values rather than the lower AI allocation suggested elsewhere. Human is diffuse around the shared bands. Record review as a structural local variant and a directional counterexample.
genres.legal: AI spans a somewhat higher adjectival band with several low-adverb configurations; Human also occupies the shared adverb/advmod band. Near-zero adverb POS with nonzero advmod and broad overlapping points remain in the graph. The joint allocation is a lead, not a class boundary.
genres.abstracts: AI extends farther along the adjective/amod band while its adverb/advmod response occupies a lower region and a visible near-zero-adverb strip. Human has a broader and generally higher adverbial response. Overlap remains, and the shifted adjective distribution prevents a strict conditional claim from these projections alone.
genres.articles: The two adverb/dependency bands largely overlap. The collective six-axis view suggests shifted allocation and less extreme responses, but no clearly distinct invariant surface is resolved. This is a weak genre for a strong band-shape claim.
genres.papers: AI has a wider/higher adjectival arrangement and a lower adverbial range than many Human points, but there are only 23 tuples per class. Treat it as descriptive context; no branch recurrence or independent validation is established.

character_composition.question: How do character entropy and alphabet size occupy the letter/whitespace arrangement, with case and digit context, and which shapes survive genre?
character_composition.definition_control: Character fractions share text length. Alphabet size and entropy depend on length and formatting. Do not interpret the composition boundary or formatting alone as an authorship signature.
character_composition.interaction: Letter/whitespace composition supports different entropy, alphabet-size, case and digit configurations. AI often occupies a thin composition band, but entropy responses differ by genre; formatting and shared character denominators are concrete explanations.

genres.email: AI follows a thin letter/whitespace band and compact entropy response; Human spreads across whitespace, alphabet size and case/digit configurations. Much of this plausibly reflects email/source formatting.
genres.review: AI has a thin composition segment and several entropy levels; Human is broader. The levels are local and should not be made a universal entropy formula.
genres.legal: AI entropy varies markedly within a narrow letter-fraction region and includes high-case points. Human also has case-sensitive entropy changes. This contradicts a single narrow AI entropy rule.
genres.abstracts: Both classes show falling entropy with increasing letter share, although their whitespace support differs. The shared slope is not a class-specific discovery.
genres.articles: AI entropy is relatively flat over its letter-fraction range while Human has a broader, somewhat falling response. Source formatting and alphabet composition remain unresolved.
genres.papers: One large Human alphabet/entropy outlier affects the full range; AI is more compact, but only 23-per-class examples are available. Retain it as a source/formatting control.
